Argued that electoral reform should support fair, open and transparent elections and grassroots participation, while supporting amendments to raise donation disclosure and donation caps to $5,000 and $50,000; later debate criticised the bill as a rushed arrangement that could entrench major-party power and reduce scrutiny.

Moved to suspend standing orders so debate on the Electoral Legislation Amendment (Electoral Reform) Bill 2024 could continue without time limitation, arguing that the bill entrenched major-party control and required greater accountability and scrutiny.

Moved government amendments to the Electoral Legislation Amendment (Electoral Reform) Bill 2024 concerning peak representative bodies, gifts, federal accounts, election funding eligibility and the pre-poll voting period; the proposed pre-poll changes were negatived, and support was recorded for specified amendments.
